repository.name: @webex/internal-plugin-conversation
repository.purpose: Internal Webex JS SDK plugin for the Webex conversation service. Registers webex.internal.conversation to create, read, and update conversations and activities, encrypts outbound and decrypts inbound conversation objects through KMS payload transforms, shares files through ShareActivity, and reads activities in thread order.

glossary.definition: A Webex space, addressed by its conversation-service URL.
glossary.notes: getConvoUrl resolves the URL from url, cluster plus id, or the in-process id cache.

glossary.definition: One verb applied to an object in a conversation target.
glossary.notes: Built by prepare and sent by submit.

glossary.definition: An activity that is or could be a thread parent.
A child activity whose parent has not been fetched.
glossary.notes: Thread ordering keeps children for the generator lifetime so orphans are not lost.

glossary.definition: KMS resource object URL bound to a conversation.
glossary.notes: Substituted for the KRO placeholder token in KMS message URIs.

glossary.definition: Encrypted reference to uploaded content carrying its key and location.
glossary.notes: Created by the encryption plugin or node-scr for GIFs.

evidence_rules.requirement: Emit a command only when its script exists in package.json and the workspace-scoped invocation was verified.
Emit an export name only when it is exported from src/index.js and reachable through main or devMain.
Ground every behavior claim in the implementation and state separately whether a test observes it.
evidence_rules.notes: Commit history is not acceptable rationale evidence for this package.

evidence_rules.requirement: Never ship a template placeholder in a generated document; replace it with verified repository evidence or surface the gap as a blocking question.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not call encryption directly from a conversation method.
negative_guidance.why: Encryption belongs to the outbound payload transform; calling it twice double-encrypts or bypasses key selection.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not add an objectType or verb without its named transform.
negative_guidance.why: Unknown transform names are silent no-ops in the WebexCore payload transformer, so content would leave unencrypted.
Messages are end-to-end encrypted; existing warnings log only reasons and URLs.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not change the reaction HMAC input order.
negative_guidance.why: Other Webex clients compute the same HMAC to deduplicate reactions.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not cite commit or pull-request history as rationale for current behavior.
negative_guidance.why: The package owner chose code-only evidence during onboarding.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat src/activity-threading.md as authoritative.
negative_guidance.why: It is a retained, superseded note; several statements no longer match the code. src/docs/README.md is canonical.

high.expectation: The claim is backed by a src file and a test that observes it, and the affected specification sections are updated in the same change.

medium.expectation: Implementation evidence exists but no test observes the behavior, as with key-rotation retries. Record the gap in the Verification section.

low.expectation: Neither code nor tests establish the fact. Stop and ask the package owner.

fallback_rules: When code and this context disagree, the code wins; correct the context and the affected specification sections in the same change.
When a fact cannot be established from src, tests, or package.json, stop and ask the package owner rather than inferring it from commit history.
When a required command is missing, say so and stop; do not substitute a plausible alternative.
When a change would alter an export or a transform name, treat it as breaking until a dependent-package review proves otherwise.
